cities.base: Central Beijing, walkable to the Forbidden City and Temple of Heaven, good base for both the arrival days and the return
cities.name: Beijing

cities.base: Inside or near the City Wall, close to the Muslim Quarter and a short drive from the Terracotta Army
cities.name: Xi'an

places.name: Drum Tower
places.note: Faces the Bell Tower, marks the entrance to the Muslim Quarter. Pair it with the food crawl rather than visiting separately, the drum performance times are posted at the entrance if you want to catch one.

places.name: Xi'an City Wall, night section near Anyuanmen
places.note: A quieter stretch of the wall away from the main tourist gates, lit up at night, worth a walk if you want the wall without the bike crowd. No separate ticket if you're already inside the loop.

places.name: De Fa Chang Restaurant
places.note: Old-school dumpling restaurant known for its dumpling banquet, sit-down alternative to the street stalls if you want a table and a menu rather than eating standing up.

places.name: Beiyuanmen Muslim Quarter Street
places.note: The main artery, loud, crowded, and touristy but the food is real: yangrou paomo, roujiamo, biangbiang noodles, persimmon cakes. Go hungry and share plates.

places.name: Xi'an City Wall, South Gate (Yongningmen)
places.note: Best entry point for the bike loop, rent here, ride the full 14km circuit or just a stretch near sunset when the light hits the ramparts.

places.name: Huaqing Palace
places.note: Hot spring complex tied to Tang dynasty emperor Xuanzong and Yang Guifei, plus the site where Chiang Kai-shek was detained in 1936. Fine if you're already out this way and have extra time, not essential.

places.name: Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum Mound
places.note: The actual burial mound of the emperor, unexcavated, a few kilometers from the pits. Just a grassy hill with a viewing platform, skip unless you have real time to spare, most people don't make it here on a half-day visit.

places.name: Bronze Chariots Exhibition Hall
places.note: Two full-size bronze chariots and horses found near the tomb mound, 20 minutes on the way between pits. The 2026 ticket page does not list this hall among what the 120 yuan ticket covers, so check the price at the gate.

places.name: Terracotta Army, Pit 3
places.note: The smallest pit, thought to be the army's command post, a 30 minute stop. No charge beyond the 120 yuan Terracotta Army ticket, which covers Pits 1, 2 and 3, Lishan Garden and the shuttle bus; last entry 16:30 from 16 November.

places.name: Terracotta Army Museum, Pit 1
places.note: The hangar of soldiers everyone pictures; go straight here before the tour groups, then work back through Pits 2 and 3. 120 yuan covers all three pits and the shuttle, booked with your passport number for one entry on the chosen date.

places.name: Gubei Water Town (Simatai)
places.note: A reconstructed canal town near the Simatai wall section, sometimes pitched as a Mutianyu add-on. Too far out of the way to combine with a single day trip from Beijing, skip on this itinerary.

places.name: Mutianyu Visitor Center and Ticket Office
places.note: Where cars and tour buses drop off, buy or collect tickets here before heading up. Basic facilities, nothing more.

places.name: Mutianyu Roadside Fruit and Snack Stalls
places.note: Persimmons, walnuts, and grilled corn sold by locals along the entrance road. Fine for a snack, do not expect much variety.

places.name: The Schoolhouse at Mutianyu
places.note: Converted village schoolhouse turned restaurant and cafe, does a decent western-friendly lunch if you want a real sit-down break before or after the wall.

places.name: Mutianyu Village
places.note: The small settlement at the foot of the wall, a scatter of guesthouses and farm stalls. Nothing to plan around but worth a wander while waiting for a ride.

places.name: Mutianyu Toboggan Slide
places.note: A metal slide down the mountainside back to the entrance. Genuinely fun, not just a gimmick, but lines form fast after 11am.

places.name: Mutianyu Cable Car
places.note: Takes you up to tower 14 and saves the steepest climb, 140 yuan in 2026. Combine with the toboggan for the way down, faster and more fun than walking.

places.name: Datang Everbright City / Big Goose Pagoda light show
places.note: Skip. Fountain and light show plaza next to the pagoda, packed with crowds and LED screens, feels more like a shopping mall event than anything distinctly Xi'an. Fine to walk through on your way somewhere else, not worth carving out time for.

places.name: Forest of Stone Steles Museum (Beilin Museum)
places.note: Hundreds of engraved stone tablets, some over a thousand years old, big draw for calligraphy enthusiasts. Niche compared to the wall or the Army, worth it only if you have real slack in the schedule, otherwise skip.
places.neighborhood: near City Wall, South Gate area

places.name: Tang Dynasty Show and Dinner
places.note: Costumed dance and music performance styled after Tang court entertainment, dumpling banquet dinner usually bundled in. Polished and aimed squarely at tour groups, fine if you want an easy evening out but skip if you'd rather spend that time in the Muslim Quarter for less money.

places.name: De Fa Chang (Muslim Quarter branch)
places.note: Reliable sit-down spot for yang rou pao mo if you want the dish properly plated rather than from a stall, you tear the flatbread into the bowl yourself before it's returned to the kitchen. Useful if the street stalls feel too chaotic for a full meal.

places.name: Great Mosque of Xi'an
places.note: One of China's oldest mosques, built in Chinese temple architectural style rather than the domes-and-minarets look, so it reads more like a garden courtyard complex. Quiet break from the food crawl chaos a few minutes' walk away, still an active place of worship so dress and behave accordingly.

places.name: Shaanxi History Museum
places.note: Free but capped daily entry, get tickets online or queue early morning. Good context before or after the Terracotta Army, bronzes and Tang dynasty artifacts. Closed Mondays. Worth it on a day you're not rushing to fit in the Army and the wall both.

places.name: Bell Tower
places.note: Ming dynasty tower sitting on a traffic roundabout in the dead center of the city. Interior is modest, worth a quick stop mainly if you're already walking between the wall and the Muslim Quarter, not worth a special trip on its own.

places.name: Big Wild Goose Pagoda
places.note: Tang dynasty brick pagoda, built to house Buddhist sutras brought back from India by the monk Xuanzang. You can pay extra to climb it but the views aren't dramatic, the square and fountain plaza outside in early evening is the nicer reason to come.

places.name: Muslim Quarter (Huimin Jie / Beiyuanmen)
places.note: Dense street food strip, yang rou pao mo (lamb flatbread soup), roujiamo, biangbiang noodles, persimmon cakes. Loud, crowded, and touristy by day, better after dark when it's lit up and locals are out too. Stalls on the main drag charge tourist prices; the side alleys are cheaper.

places.name: Xi'an City Wall
places.note: Complete Ming-era wall, one of the few in China you can bike the full loop of (about 13-14km, but renting for a shorter stretch near South Gate is enough). Bike rental is separate from entry. Sunset light on the ramparts is the reason to do it late in the day rather than midday.

places.name: Terracotta Army (Museum of Qin Terracotta Warriors and Horses)
places.note: Pit 1 is the money shot, Pits 2 and 3 are broken pieces and lab work; 120 yuan covers all three, 08:30 to 18:00 with last entry 16:30 in winter. An hour's drive each way, go early, and walk past the jade and replica shops on the way out.

places.name: Quanjude Roast Duck (Qianmen)
places.note: The original Beijing duck house, dating to 1864, at 180 to 260 yuan a head (Jul 2026). Touristy and pricier than neighbourhood spots, but the duck is the real thing and worth one night of the trip.

places.name: Wangfujing Snack Street
places.note: Skewers of scorpion and starfish are for the cameras, not the eating. Fine for a quick look but the actual food quality is better in the hutong noodle shops nearby.

places.name: Beijing Olympic Park (Bird's Nest and Water Cube)
places.note: Nothing to actually do beyond photographing the exteriors from outside the fence unless you pay extra to go in. Not worth a half day on a six day trip.

places.name: 798 Art District
places.note: Converted factory complex of galleries and street art, a good rainy-day option. Entry to the district is free and it never closes, but individual museums and shows may charge; most open about 10:00 to 18:00 and some close Mondays.

places.name: Houhai Lake
places.note: Bar-lined lake, good for an evening walk and a drink after the hutongs. Loud and touristy on weekends, quieter midweek.

places.name: Nanluoguxiang and surrounding hutongs
places.note: The main lane itself is touristy and full of shops, duck into the quieter side alleys off it for the actual courtyard housing and neighborhood feel.

places.name: Summer Palace
places.note: Combined ticket covers the halls plus grounds. Walk Kunming Lake's shore and the Long Corridor, boat rental available if you want to be on the water instead.

places.name: Temple of Heaven
places.note: The 34 yuan combo covers the park and the inner halls. Go early for locals doing tai chi and fan dancing before the tour groups; one 2026 guide says it stays open to 22:00, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Badaling Great Wall
places.note: Closest section to Beijing but a mob scene most of the year, shoulder to shoulder on the wall. 40 yuan, with a reservation wanted 1 to 7 days ahead; Mutianyu is worth the extra drive time.

places.name: Mutianyu Great Wall
places.note: Entrance about 10 dollars, then 15 yuan for the shuttle and 140 yuan for the cable car (2026). Less crowded than Badaling but fills by midday, so go early; about 1.5 hours each way from central Beijing.

places.name: Tiananmen Square
places.note: Security screening to enter the square itself, bring passport. Pairs naturally with the Forbidden City walk since they sit back to back.

places.name: Forbidden City
places.note: 60 yuan April to October, 40 November to March; tickets release 7 days ahead at 20:00 Beijing time and often sell out. Book with your passport number, bring the passport to the gate, and read up beforehand instead of queuing for the audio guide.

places.name: Muslim Quarter
places.note: Street food crawl territory, budget $15-20 to do it properly.

places.name: Siji Minfu Roast Duck (Nanchizi)
places.note: Peking duck five minutes from the Forbidden City's north-east corner, 4.4 on Google. Half a duck for two or three is 159 yuan and a whole one 259; plan on 130 to 180 a head (Jul 2026), 10:30 to 21:30 daily.

places.name: Donglaishun Wangfujing
places.note: Old Beijing mutton hotpot in copper pots, 11:00 to 22:00. About 100 to 130 yuan a head (Jul 2026), quoted for the flagship on the 5th floor of Beijing APM, 138 Wangfujing; this point is matched by street only, so confirm the branch.

places.name: First Noodle under the Sun
places.note: Biangbiang and other Shaanxi noodles, 10:00 to 22:00 daily. The 45 to 60 yuan a head (May 2026) is quoted for the chain's main branch by the Big Wild Goose Pagoda; this is the Hanguang Road branch, so prices may differ.

places.name: Biang Biang Noodles (80 Nanyuanmen)
places.note: Wide hand-pulled biangbiang noodles, the Shaanxi dish with the 58-stroke character, about 1 km south of the Bell Tower. Around 25 yuan a head (May 2026), 10:00 to 22:00 daily; 4.2 on Google.
places.neighborhood: Beilin, Nanyuanmen, south of the Bell Tower

places.name: Lama Temple (Yonghegong)
places.note: Tibetan Buddhist temple in a former Qing prince's residence, 4.7 on 1,235 reviews. 25 yuan at the window with your passport or on Trip.com; one listing says 17:00 closing, another 16:30, so hours vary, check.

places.name: National Museum of China
places.note: Free, but book a timed slot 1 to 7 days ahead on the official site or WeChat and bring your passport. The Ancient China exhibition is the core; closed Mondays, and one guide says 17:00 closing, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Capital Museum
places.note: Beijing's own history plus bronzes, jade and ceramics, 09:00 to 16:00, closed Mondays. Reviews say free, but a booking site sells entry at 6 dollars, so check the price before you go.

places.name: Beihai Park
places.note: Liao-to-Qing imperial garden around a lake, with the White Dagoba on its island. 5 yuan from November to March, 15 for the combo, 06:30 to 20:00 with last entry 19:30; 06:00 to 21:00 from April.

places.name: Prince Gong Mansion
places.note: Qing mansion and garden near Houhai, 4.4 on Google. 40 yuan, half for seniors and students, 08:30 to 16:30, closed Mondays; the hours page is undated, so verify before travel.

outings.why: The imperial palace complex plus the square out front, best in the afternoon once you've slept off the flight; buy the timed ticket online in advance since they cap daily visitors.
outings.name: Forbidden City and Tiananmen Square

outings.why: A day trip with about 1.5 hours' drive each way plus the cable car up, less crowded than Badaling but still fills by midday so go early.
outings.name: Great Wall at Mutianyu
outings.season: year-round, snow in winter if you don't mind the cold

outings.why: Half a day including the hour's drive out from the city; the museum shop pressure to buy is heavy, skip it.
outings.name: Terracotta Army

outings.why: Rent a bike and ride the top of the wall, best near sunset.
outings.name: Xi'an City Wall bike ride

outings.why: An evening street food crawl, budget $15-20 for a proper go at it.
outings.name: Muslim Quarter food crawl

outings.why: A quieter add-on if there's daylight left after the Muslim Quarter or before it.
outings.name: Big Wild Goose Pagoda

outings.why: Temple of Heaven park in the morning, then a hutong walk and dinner in the evening.
outings.name: Temple of Heaven morning and hutong walk

outings.why: Half a day including a walk around Kunming Lake, a calmer close to the trip before flying home.
outings.name: Summer Palace

destination.name: China: Beijing & Xi'an
destination.pitch: A week is really Beijing bookending a Terracotta Army detour to Xi'an, and that's the right-sized trip for a first visit.
destination.caveat: Two nights in Xi'an means one full day and two half days, so a flight delay costs you the Terracotta Army. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Beijing's scale and hutongs versus Xi'an's walled old city give you two very different urban days.
because.food: The Muslim Quarter food crawl alone is worth the Xi'an detour.
because.culture: Forbidden City, Temple of Heaven and the Terracotta Army in one trip is as dense a history dose as you'll get anywhere.
because.adventure: Toboggan down off the Wall at Mutianyu if you want a bit of silliness with your history.
because.exploration: Xi'an City Wall by bike is a different way to see a city than walking it.
